title: Singapore's Exposure to China's Belt and Road Initiative
what_it_is: Singapore's Exposure to China's Belt and Road Initiative

sections.label: Belt and Road Singapore companies
sections.summary: The Belt and Road is a mutually beneficial initiative encouraging regional economic integration, with Singapore companies' engagements so far not large but expected to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Who is answering on behalf of the front bench?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: It is a mutually beneficial initiative that will encourage further economic integration, infrastructural cooperation and people-to-people linkages among countries in the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China's Singapore branch recently signed an MOU with Singapore Business Federation to extend up to RMB 50 billion in funding to Singapore companies for infrastructure projects across Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Given that the Belt and Road is a relatively recent initiative, Singapore companies' direct engagements so far are not large but, I am sure will grow.

sections.label: China slowdown Singapore financial system
sections.summary: The slowdown poses no material risk to Singapore's financial system or economy, and cooperation with Chinese authorities recognises China's interest in stability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The slowdown does not pose any material risk for the Singapore financial system or economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As China grows and becomes more integrated with the world, its capital outflows and investments abroad will likely grow steadily over the long term and the RMB will become more internationalised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Our cooperation with the Chinese authorities, monetary and financial regulators, fully recognises China's interest in ensuring that the journey is a stable and orderly one, and in guarding against sudden and excessive capital outflows.

sections.label: Private entities Belt and Road investments
sections.summary: Belt and Road investments will be made by private entities, not the Government, and they must assess viability and abide by local laws and governance standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If there are investments in Belt and Road initiatives – and we are really at a nascent stage of doing this the investments will not be made by the Government, but by private entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They have to do their own calculations on the viability of the projects, whether they will succeed, whether they bring greater benefits to the region and the host country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They have to abide by local laws and abide by very high standards of governance expected of all our corporates that invest overseas.
